about.title: Expedition Naturalist & Wildlife Photojournalist
about.credentials: Official Member: International League of Conservation Photographers (Affiliate) • National Geographic Contributor
about.bioParagraph: I am Suban Dahit, a Nepali wildlife photojournalist dedicated to documenting the fragile altitudinal gradients of the Himalayas and the lowland Terai. From dense subtropical Sal riverbanks (68m) to frost-shattered Tibetan plateau passes (5,400m), my work bridges rigorous scientific observation and fine art storytelling.
about.manifestoQuote: “We do not stage moments in the wild; we endure the freeze, the damp, and weeks of absolute stillness until the wild chooses to reveal itself.”
about.manifestoText: Wildlife photography is not about conquest or lens specs—it is about biological empathy. When an apex predator looks into your lens, it is calculating whether your presence threatens its territory. Our strict policy is that when we pack up our hides, the animal must never have altered its feeding, mating, or resting habits because of us.

ethics.title: Zero Baiting & Calling
ethics.description: Every recorded frame depicts 100% natural, unmanipulated wildlife behavior. We never use carcass bait, live lures, acoustic calls, or salt licks to attract animals.

ethics.title: Non-Disruptive Drone Ban
ethics.description: Complete 100% exclusion of aerial drones in active buffer sanctuaries. Aerial prop noise induces acute cortisol stress spikes in big cats and avian raptors.

ethics.title: GPS Coordinate Obfuscation
ethics.description: Raw telemetry and precise nest coordinates of critically endangered species are systematically scrubbed and encrypted to prevent illegal poaching exploitation.

ethics.title: The 10% Community Royalty
ethics.description: Exactly 10% of every print acquisition, publication fee, and licensing contract goes directly into community anti-poaching patrols (CBAPU) and park ranger welfare.

expeditions.desc: Documenting the endangered Red Panda navigating ancient moss-covered oak and rhododendron canopies in torrential mid-monsoon rainfall without artificial light.
expeditions.title: Monsoon Mist: Cloud Forest Red Panda Study

expeditions.desc: Four weeks in camouflaged drift-wood blinds along sub-zero gravel crossings, resulting in the iconic direct ocular portrait of dominant male T-14 at 48 meters.
expeditions.title: The Stare: Royal Bengal Tiger Riverbank Watch

expeditions.desc: Tracking bearded vultures and Himalayan griffons riding gale-force mountain vortexes and thermal updrafts across sheer limestone red canyons.
expeditions.title: Wings Across the Himalaya: Lammergeier Dynamics

expeditions.desc: A grueling 38-day sub-zero winter bivouac across jagged moraines, capturing the solitary phantom traversing wind-blasted ridges during snow squalls.
expeditions.title: Monarchs of the High Passes: Winter Snow Leopard
